title: Inquest urges Surrey RCMP to screen for alcohol withdrawal
article: A coroners court jury has recommended that the Surrey RCMP and city staff be more mindful of prisoners' behavioural changes, following an inquest into the death of 58-year-old Surinder Singh Mahli.

Mahli died on Dec. 30, 2011 at Surrey Memorial Hospital. He was arrested Dec. 23 for breaching a court order, and taken to hospital Dec. 26 after he was found lying unresponsive on the floor of his cell.

The inquest, held last week in Burnaby, concluded that the cause of Mahli's death was chronic alcohol abuse, with heart disease as a significant factor. The jury recommended that the Surrey RCMP obtain a "screening tool" to detect alcohol withdrawal, "as this can be a serious issue and would be important to be identified early on to prevent any serious consequences."

The jury also recommended the RCMP and the City of Surrey log changes in prisoner behaviour in a written report at the end of every working shift, with notations to be passed on to a manager who can follow up.
The jury recommended the logbook be kept where all employees can see it.
The jury also said a nurse or medical practitioner should be at the cells 24 hours a day to assess prisoners upon arrival and during their stay.
